description: carculator is the Paul Scherrer Institute Technology Assessment group's parameterised Python model for life-cycle assessment of passenger cars and light-duty vehicles. It contains vehicle energy calculations, pollutant and noise emissions, cost indicators and inventory export to Brightway or SimaPro. Inputs specify vehicle technology, size, driving cycle and background energy scenarios; outputs include environmental impacts and uncertainty estimates. Coverage follows the supplied vehicle and country assumptions, with current and future years represented by time-specific inventories. Source is free under BSD-3-Clause, while external inventory databases retain their own terms. A limitation is that future impacts depend on scenario assumptions, not observations. Monte Carlo results preserve modelled parameter relationships but do not remove those uncertainties. The model supports transport electrification and energy-demand simulations. Brightway (platform-brightway-lca) is a related assessment platform. The README cites its methodological basis in a 2018 battery-vehicle footprint study.
inputs: Vehicle, driving-cycle and background inventory parameters
